reason: E1 mentions segregation in as-cast refractory HEAs but does not demonstrate that homogenization dissolves it or improves strength. E2 applies a 2100°C/2h homogenization to different alloys and discusses strength, but does not directly compare as-cast vs. homogenized states or quantify the improvement. The key premises about the effect of homogenization on segregation, strengthening, and yield strength improvement are therefore not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: As-cast refractory HEAs exhibit compositional segregations and nonuniform element distributions
Ultra-high-temperature homogenization (2100°C, 2h) dissolves segregated phases and yields a uniform single-phase BCC solid solution
A uniform, segregation-free BCC microstructure enhances solid-solution strengthening and inhibits dislocation glide at high temperatures
Homogenized refractory HEAs show higher yield strength at elevated temperatures (800–1200°C) compared to as-cast counterparts
